blocks.text: Berkley Terraces — 999 Berkley Road (District of North Vancouver)

A 3-storey, 31-unit low-rise; the building directory states 31 units and amenities of elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and swirlpool/hot tub. Year-built conflict to flag: the directory states built 1989, while current listings for units in the building state built 1992. A current listing describes freehold strata title, clubhouse, exercise centre and recreation facilities. Published restrictions: the directory states age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions, and rentals not allowed — the "rentals not allowed" line is void for long-term rentals since November 24, 2022, and a current listing states it more narrowly as "no rentals except to immediate family," which is the same void restriction in another form.
Baden Park (Yew and Seymour garden-flat collections) — Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway, addresses including 948, 954, 956 and 968 Lytton Street (District of North Vancouver)

GEOGRAPHY / MLS-CLASSIFICATION FLAG: this new Anthem community sits at the pocket's south edge, and MLS listings for the same community are split between sub-areas — some units are classified Blueridge NV and others Windsor Park NV. The project is a 6.25-acre master-planned community by Anthem Properties; one project source states 119 condominiums, 133 townhomes and 89 rental apartments at build-out, and a project-listing source states 341 total homes. Current listings describe the garden flats as apartment/condo form, freehold strata, built 2026, wood-frame construction. Because completions are in 2026, early purchases may still be on developer contracts — REDMA applies to those.
Streets, schools and getting around Blueridge

items.t: Blueridge is the District of North Vancouver's Seymour-community residential pocket north of Mount Seymour Parkway, east of the Seymour River, on the Berkley Road / Hyannis Drive street grid below Mount Seymour. Confirmed street anchors are Sechelt Drive, Hyannis Drive, Berkley Road, Carnation Street and Emerson Court, between Mount Seymour Parkway in the south and the Seymour River side in the west.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: there is almost none. The stock sits in exactly two places: one older low-rise on Berkley Road in the middle of the pocket (Berkley Terraces), and one brand-new master-planned community at the pocket's south edge on Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway. Everything else in the pocket is detached houses.

Transit anchor: TransLink route 214 (Blueridge / Phibbs Exchange / Burrard Station) runs from Sechelt Drive at Hyannis Drive via Sechelt Drive, Berkley Road, Carnation Street, Emerson Court, Mount Seymour Parkway, Riverside Drive, Old Dollarton Road, Dollarton Highway and Main Street to Phibbs Exchange, with some trips continuing to Burrard Station. The R2 RapidBus connects at Phibbs Exchange and, since September 7, 2026, runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Anchors inside and beside the area: Blueridge Elementary, 2650 Bronte Drive, and Seymour Heights Elementary, 2640 Carnation Street, are both in the pocket; Windsor Secondary, 931 Broadview Drive, is the Seymour secondary beside the area; Parkgate Village, Parkgate Community Centre (3625 Banff Court) and the Parkgate library branch (3675 Banff Court) are north-east of the area; Mount Seymour Provincial Park rises behind the community.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Blueridge

items.t: Slope hazard — the Berkley-side check: District landslide work names the Berkley escarpment as an area with landslide risk; after the January 19, 2005 landslide on the Berkley Escarpment the District began proactive District-wide hazard management, and its Landslide Risk Assessment was updated in 2026. Berkley Terraces sits on Berkley Road — pull the District GeoWeb hazard layers for the complex's parcel before subject removal. District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B also sets Streamside, Wildfire, Creek and Slope Hazard Development Permit Areas.

District tax timing: District of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value.

One new community is filed under two different neighbourhoods. Baden Park's Lytton Street units appear on MLS under both Blueridge NV and Windsor Park NV — a search, an alert or a comparable set built on only one name silently drops half the community.

Baden Park mixes three tenures on one site. At build-out the project source states 119 condominiums, 133 townhomes and 89 rental apartments in one master-planned community — a "for sale" sign at the site does not tell a buyer which tenure a given building is.

The 2005 slide still shapes diligence on the west side of the pocket. The January 19, 2005 Berkley Escarpment landslide is the reason the District runs proactive landslide management and updated its Landslide Risk Assessment in 2026 — Berkley Road addresses carry a hazard-layer check that most North Shore condo pockets do not.

The fastest bus on the North Shore now connects at this pocket's exchange. Since September 7, 2026 the R2 RapidBus runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station — Blueridge's route 214 feeds Phibbs, so the pocket's downtown and Burnaby routes both changed that day.

blocks.text: Municipality, stated first because it decides the bylaws: Blueridge is in the District of North Vancouver — OCP Bylaw No. 7900 / Zoning Bylaw No. 3210. The City of North Vancouver's OCP 8400 / Zoning 6700 belong to the City (Calverhall, Central Lonsdale) and are never imported here. Both bases are stated; the standalone count below is zero, honestly.
Streets, schools and getting around Blueridge

items.t: Where the stock sits: detached houses across the pocket; the only apartment-condo building inside the pocket is Berkley Terraces on Berkley Road, and the only townhome-form product is the Baden Park component at the pocket's south edge on Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway. Attached forms otherwise concentrate near Parkgate Village and along Mount Seymour Parkway, outside this pocket.

Blueridge is in the District of North Vancouver, which is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's FVR + GVR September 2026 reports — no North Vancouver section, sub-area rows or community medians exist for it, and no other stats source is substituted.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 214 (Blueridge / Phibbs Exchange / Burrard Station) runs from Sechelt Drive at Hyannis Drive via Sechelt Drive, Berkley Road, Carnation Street, Emerson Court, Mount Seymour Parkway, Riverside Drive, Old Dollarton Road, Dollarton Highway and Main Street to Phibbs Exchange, with some trips continuing to Burrard Station; the R2 RapidBus connects at Phibbs Exchange and, since September 7, 2026, runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station. Mount Seymour Parkway is the main east–west road at the south side.

Schools: SD44 catchments are address-based, with elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only and no middle tier. Blueridge Elementary, 2650 Bronte Drive, and Seymour Heights Elementary, 2640 Carnation Street, are both in the pocket, and Windsor Secondary, 931 Broadview Drive, is the Seymour secondary beside the area.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Blueridge

items.t: Form B diligence (strata purchases — Berkley Terraces and any Baden Park strata unit): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a 2026 Baden Park unit, establish first whether it is a developer sale (disclosure statement route) or a resale (Form B route).

District plans and zoning — the DISTRICT pair only: District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 7900 and Zoning Bylaw No. 3210, Section 525 (Bylaw 8799): R1 minimum lot 4,000 m² (30 m width, 34 m depth); R2 minimum lot 660 m² (18 m width, 34 m depth), with modifiers R2(S1) 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 lot allows a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house. The Seymour Local Plan maintains Blueridge's predominantly single-family character.

SSMUH / suites as the District states them: since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary; the District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop. A suite or coach house is a fee-simple second unit on a house lot — never a townhouse complex.

Hazard permits — the Berkley-side check: District landslide work names the Berkley escarpment as an area with landslide risk; after the January 19, 2005 landslide on the Berkley Escarpment the District began proactive District-wide hazard management, and its Landslide Risk Assessment was updated in 2026. OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m. Berkley Road addresses carry this check.

District taxes: District of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value; combined single-family utilities are $2,571.20 in 2026 (water $932.80; sewer/drainage $1,255.60).
Blueridge attached supply is tiny, but it is not zero — its townhome share is a component, not a complex.

One new community is filed under two different neighbourhoods (checked Nov 1, 2026). Baden Park's Lytton Street units appear on MLS under both Blueridge NV and Windsor Park NV, and fresh listings for its Cove townhomes use Windsor Park NV while a Seymour townhouse listing at 954 Lytton Street uses Blueridge NV — a search, alert or comparable set built on only one name silently drops part of the community.

Baden Park mixes three tenures on one site (checked Nov 1, 2026). At build-out the project source states 119 condominiums, 133 townhomes and 89 rental apartments in one master-planned community — a "for sale" sign at the site does not tell a buyer which tenure a given building is.

The 2005 slide still shapes diligence on the west side of the pocket. The January 19, 2005 Berkley Escarpment landslide is the reason the District runs proactive landslide management and updated its Landslide Risk Assessment in 2026 — Berkley Road addresses carry a hazard-layer check most North Shore pockets do not.

The mountain is the amenity, and it is a provincial park. Mount Seymour Provincial Park (established 1936) rises behind the Seymour community north-east of Blueridge, and the Mt Seymour ski area inside it operates under an 81-hectare controlled recreation area with 39 runs, 12 of them lit for night skiing — up Mount Seymour Parkway from every Lytton Street and Berkley Road home.

No ALR percentage split is stated; check any parcel on ALC mapping.

Hazard position — the defining check: District work names the Berkley escarpment as an area with landslide risk; after the January 19, 2005 landslide on the Berkley Escarpment the District began proactive District-wide management of landslide and other natural hazards, and its Landslide Risk Assessment was updated in 2026. OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m.
Baden Park (Lytton Street at Mount Seymour Parkway) — cross-reference only; not counted in this area.

No other named bare-land development, assembly, development site or rezoning proposal inside Blueridge is documented: — none is carried as for-sale inventory. The governing plan position is the opposite of speculative: the Seymour Local Plan manages slow, limited growth to protect the area's forested character and maintains the predominantly single-family character of established neighbourhoods such as Blueridge.

Historic subdivision fabric = built lot fabric, not offerings: the Berkley Road / Hyannis Drive streets are established fee-simple lot fabric documented above; no historic subdivision is presented as a lot offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Blueridge

items.t: Nearby areas: Seymour Heights (south-west, sharing the school community), Windsor Park / Windsor Secondary (south-east), Parkgate Village and Mount Seymour (north-east, up Mount Seymour Parkway), Indian River / Dorothy Lynas (north), and Lynn Valley (west, across the Seymour River).

Parks, recreation and services: Mount Seymour Provincial Park (established 1936) rises behind the Seymour community north-east of Blueridge, with hiking and mountain-bike trails (Baden-Powell, Old Buck) and the Mt Seymour ski area (39 runs, 12 night-lit) inside an 81-hectare controlled recreation area. Parkgate Community Centre, 3625 Banff Court, and the Parkgate branch library, 3675 Banff Court, are north-east of the area; Ron Andrews Community Recreation Centre, 931 Lytton Street, is beside Windsor Secondary south of the area. Northlands Golf Course, 3400 Anne Macdonald Way, is District-owned and public; Seymour Golf & Country Club is private, at 3723 Mount Seymour Parkway. Health care: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver; North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2nd floor, 221 West Esplanade. Shopping: Parkgate Village is one of the District's six Village Centres under the OCP and is the Seymour community's shopping centre.

Roads and transit: Mount Seymour Parkway is the main east–west road at the south side; Berkley Road and Hyannis Drive are the main roads inside the area. TransLink route 214 (Blueridge / Phibbs Exchange / Burrard Station) runs from Sechelt Drive at Hyannis Drive via Sechelt Drive, Berkley Road, Carnation Street, Emerson Court, Mount Seymour Parkway, Riverside Drive, Old Dollarton Road, Dollarton Highway and Main Street to Phibbs Exchange, with some trips continuing to Burrard Station; the R2 RapidBus connects at Phibbs Exchange and, since September 7, 2026, runs one-seat from Park Royal through Lonsdale Quay and Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station.

Schools: SD44 catchments are address-based; SD44 has elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only, with no middle tier. Blueridge Elementary, 2650 Bronte Drive, and Seymour Heights Elementary, 2640 Carnation Street, are both in the pocket, and Windsor Secondary, 931 Broadview Drive, is the secondary school in the Seymour community beside the area.
District context only: the District's 2021 Census population was 88,168, in 32,700 of 34,179 total private dwellings, on 160.66 km².

parts.t: The rules that apply across Surrey (zoning, suites, strata, land and taxes) are on one page:
buying a home in Surrey: the rules

items.t: Zoning — District Zoning Bylaw No. 3210, Section 525 (Bylaw 8799): the R1/R2 minimum-lot ladder in; an R2 lot allows a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house. Since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary.

OCP — District Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 7900: the District plan covering the area, including Schedule B Development Permit Areas (Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard, Slope Hazard); the Seymour Local Plan sits under it for this community and protects Blueridge's single-family character. The City of North Vancouver's OCP 8400 is a different municipality's plan and is never imported here.

SSMUH as the District states it: the District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop — check the lot's classification before marketing density, because the Seymour Local Plan's limited-growth position still shapes what is realistic here.

Hazard Development Permits (District frame — the live Blueridge checks): OCP Schedule B permit areas — slope, creek, streamside, wildfire and natural-environment protection — with the Berkley escarpment landslide record (January 19, 2005 slide; proactive management since; Landslide Risk Assessment updated 2026) as the first check on Berkley-side lots; pull the GeoWeb hazard layers and budget for a geotechnical report before pricing a renovation or rebuild.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Blueridge ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

District property taxes: District of North Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value.

The plan works against density speculation here: the Seymour Local Plan deliberately limits growth and protects single-family character, so speculative multiplex land value is limited despite the District-wide suite/coach-house permission — a lot's SSMUH classification, not the headline rule, is what to price.

Flood levels here are modelled to a 2100 horizon: District GeoWeb property reports carry modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a dated, property-level figure a buyer can pull before subjects come off.

The ski hill is part of the same street grid's story: the Mt Seymour ski area operates inside Mount Seymour Provincial Park (established 1936) under an 81-hectare controlled recreation area, with 39 runs, 12 of them lit for night skiing — up the Parkway from the pocket's south edge.
